chunk_map.heading: H1 lede: The agentic engineering progression

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked every pronoun/demonstrative per chunk. Chunk 2-6 'it'/'that whole shape'/'the first'/'it'/'its surroundings' each resolve to a noun named earlier in the same chunk (the agent, task shape, a delegated task, the recurring task/one loop, a working loop). Chunk 8 'Unmeasured green' and 'the gates behind it' resolve against the same-chunk diagram caption text ('GATES AND CHECKS YOU TRUST', 'moves as fast as the gates behind it', line 82) and the parallel 'Measured gates' clause two words earlier. Chunk 9's 'Read the doors again' is a whole-deck closer callback to the 'The door is trust...' sentences named in chunks 2-6 of the SAME file, which rule 1's NOT-violations clause explicitly allows (term introduced earlier and reused). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Both external references are named by title with inline link text, not located by position: line 9 '[The AI-Native Engineering Playbook: Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly]' and line 95 '[This is getting ridiculous: I shipped 490 pull requests in June]'. No 'the opening lecture said' / positional phrasing found anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Grepped body for 'the X you did/saw/caught' shape backward-beat phrasing — none present. This is a supplementary reading, not an exercise/lecture with a module beat history to reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the file; the file is expository prose plus one diagram, no live-demo beat.

Every chunk carries a self-carrying claim standing alone: chunk 0 states the discipline, each level chunk (2-7) states the level's substance plus (for 2-6) a three-beat Moves-you-up seam, chunk 8 carries the diagram and its four defining bullets, chunk 9 states the model's unity. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked each header against its chunk's content: 'Assistance' -> 'AI helps with work already on your desk'; 'Interactive work' -> 'One conversation, one task'; 'Delegating bounded outcomes' -> 'You hand over an outcome, not a step'; 'Directing parallel sessions' -> 'You direct several sessions rather than one conversation'; 'Encoding checked loops' -> 'Recurring work becomes a loop with its own checks'; 'Improving the system' -> 'You improve the context, memory, skills, and verification'; 'Part 2: The leverage model' -> the diagram and reach/calibration bullets; 'One model, not two' -> 'The progression and the leverage model describe the same thing.' No header contradicted by its chunk.

Checked all five sub-items per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere; the only three-item list (chunk 4: 'the task, the conditions around it, and the evidence that says it is done') has three distinct concrete legs, not repeated-clause anaphora, so not the banned shape; no self-grading superlatives (no 'one of the most useful' phrasing; 'far below the multiple suggested by its pull-request count' line 95 is a stated finding, not self-praise) -- value-prop-leak subitem PASS, blocking; numeric claims (30-40 sessions, 10-15 managed, three-to-four times value) are stated plainly with no retraction pattern; no abstraction-noun stacks ('bounded-window reality'-style) found; no verb triplets with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned body for repo/maintainer dialect (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) -- none present. 'The frontier', 'the door', 'calibration', 'reach' are page-coined and page-defined vocabulary, taught in body/diagram, not repo-internal authoring dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunks 2-6 each carry exactly one bold handle ('**Moves you up:**', confirmed via grep of ## Moves you up occurrences, one per level chunk) -- within the <=1-per-slide budget. Chunk 8 carries two bold handles ('**Reach**', '**Calibration**') on two of its four bullets -- these are the diagram's own axis-label coined terms (matching the SVG axis text verbatim), each a <=2-word handle marking a defined term, not a bolded whole-sentence lead; the other two bullets in the same list are unbolded. This is a defined-term pair essential to reading the adjacent diagram, closer in kind to the rule's named-law/coined-term carve-out than to the pre-2026-07-09 every-bullet-bold monoculture the rule exists to catch. Non-blocking regardless.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: site/layouts/slides.js:237-258 handles files 'with no phases -- prework, supplementary, reference' via the `:scope > section.module` fallback and assigns supplementary files kind code 'S' (line 205: `if (id.indexOf('supplementary-') === 0) return 'Supplementary';`), so this file reaches the composed deck despite carrying no .phase--lecture/.phase--exercise wrapper. node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file <this file> confirms 9 slides counted (matches the 9 ## chunks below chunk 0), i.e. the deck sees the same chunking this verdict used.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule text scopes the imperative/phase-label vs claim split explicitly to exercise headings vs lecture headings; this file is a supplementary reading, neither type, so the split doesn't apply. Headers here ('Assistance', 'Directing parallel sessions', 'One model, not two') are noun-phrase/topic labels throughout, internally consistent with each other.
